transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-15 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Liam, Sofia, Raj, Maya (AtlasSearch)

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do a quick 45ish minute walkthrough of Hosted API embeddings and the rerank flow, then leave time for Q&A. My voice comes through okay?
[00:12] Liam (AtlasSearch): Yep, sounds good.
[00:28] Priya (Redwood): Quick agenda — embeddings API, a live demo of similarity search into a vector DB then using our rerank endpoint to reorder results, show how Console surfaces per-query latency and token cost, and finish with Redwood Optimize tips for improving cost/latency.
[01:05] Sofia: Great. high level, we currently use Elastic + a small in-house reranker. Looking to improve relevance for long-tail queries and reduce ops overhead. We have about 30M docs, embed dims 768, and avg query QPS is ~200 at peak but bursty.
[02:10] Alex: Cool, that's helpful. A couple clarifying q's — are you storing vectors in Elastic or a separate vector DB?
[02:22] Raj: Right now Elastic with the vector plugin, but scaling is a pain, and we see fuzzy matches that need reranking. Also curious about latency — we need p95 sub 120ms for search path if possible.
[03:05] Priya: Understood. For Hosted API: embeddings are a simple REST call, you can batch up to N vectors per request — batching reduces per-vector latency and cost. Our observed median embed time for 768-d vectors on hosted is ~6-12ms per vector depending on batch size and region, p95 higher, obviously. For reranker we run a lightweight scoring model that adds an extra call — typically a few tens of ms depending on model size.
[04:30] Sofia: Can the rerank be done server-side so we don't have to pull tons of text back and forth? We want to avoid sending big documents client-side.
[04:55] Jordan (Redwood): Yes — typical pattern: query -> embed -> ANN search in your vector store (we show example with Pinecone/Elastic/OpenSearch) -> take top-K candidates (K=30 typical) -> call Redwood rerank endpoint with candidate snippets and original query; rerank returns re-scored list with explain tokens and optional highlights so you can present final ranked results without moving whole doc bodies around.
[06:12] Liam: How do you pass context? Do we send raw text snippets or IDs?
[06:28] Priya: You send either; IDs plus a short snippet is common. The reranker benefits from context so 2-3 sentence snippets are enough. Also you can include metadata fields for reranker features.
[08:03] Sofia: Any constraints on token limits for rerank calls?
[08:20] Priya: Yes, we have request size limits per model — typical limit is X tokens per request, in practice keep rerank payloads under ~3-4k tokens for low latency. We can show budgeting in Console.
[10:15] Alex: Live demo time — I'll kick off a sample notebook. Sharing screen now — pull up the demo dataset (product search toy set) and the Redwood Console.
[12:03] [screen share] Alex: In the Console you can see the Embeddings explorer — here's a single query, we call /v1/embeddings, look at response dims, cosine similarity scores in a histogram. You can toggle batch size and see simulated cost per 1M requests.
[15:22] [screen share] Alex: Now hitting the search pipeline — we call the vector DB (demo uses an in-memory ANN for speed) and return top 50. Then calling /v1/rerank with the query + top50 candidate snippets. Watch the latency metrics — rerank adds about 45ms in this demo, total p50 ~85ms, p95 ~160ms because we didn't set aggressive batching and the region is eastus.
[18:40] Raj: That p95 is higher than our target, can we tune?
[18:55] Priya: Yes — Optimize recommends: 1) batch embeddings for offline indexing, 2) enable KV cache for frequent prefixes (we call it KV cash sometimes in notes), 3) lower K for rerank (top 10 instead of 50), 4) use a smaller rerank model for strict latency SLOs, or use Hybrid approach: do a lightweight filter rerank at edge and run heavy rerank async for reordering in secondary ranking.
[21:10] Sofia: About vector DBs — you said Pinecone and Elastic. If we keep using Elastic, any special config?
[21:32] Jordan: For Elastic you want to use dense_vector with approximate nearest neighbor (HNSW) settings tuned: ef_construction and ef_search tradeoff recall vs latency. For scale we often recommend separating storage tier for dense vectors and using dedicated shards. Also Redwood can route queries to different backends via policies if you want blue/green testing.
[25:00] Liam: Security items — we need SOC2, KMS for key management, audit logs, and SSO/SAML. Also data retention policies for embeddings.
[25:20] Alex: Redwood's Hosted API is SOC2 compliant, we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and audit logs surfaced in Console. For Hosted we have robust audit trails and retention controls; we'll send the security pack.
[27:45] Sofia: Does the reranker keep customer text? We need to be sure PII isn't stored.
[28:03] Priya: By default, Hosted API does not persist user payloads beyond short-term logs used for debugging, and you can opt-out of logging. For regulated use cases we recommend Redwood Private with VPC and KMS so nothing leaves your environment. We'll include that in security docs.
[32:40] Alex: Back to demo — showing example rerank API call payload and response. Response contains scores, confidence, and an explain field with token-level highlights (note: explain is optional, costs more processing). Here you can see how the top result score jumps after rerank from 0.76 to 0.92 which improved click-through in our evals.
[35:10] Sofia: How do you evaluate improvements? Do you provide eval harness?
[35:28] Jordan: Yes — Redwood Optimize has an eval runner where you can define labeled prompts, run A/B against model variants, and get metrics (NDCG, MRR, recall@k). We'll share an example eval and the sample spreadsheet.
[38:05] Raj: About cost — what are typical per-query costs for embedding + rerank? Ballpark is fine.
[38:28] Alex: Ballpark for hosted: small embed (768) plus small rerank model might be $0.0005-$0.002 per full search depending on batch and K; big variance by model size and host vs dedicated. We'll send a detailed spreadsheet with modeled QPS scenarios.
[41:12] Liam: We have concerns about vendor lock-in to Redwood rerank API. If we build pipelines around it, can we run reranks on Dedicated or Private?
[41:33] Priya: Absolutely — same API across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. You can start Hosted for quick iteration and move to Dedicated/Private once you need VPC or performance isolation.
[44:00] Sofia: Any notes on monitoring? We need per-route latency and cost breakdowns.
[44:22] Jordan: Console provides per-route, per-model dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, traces, and error buckets. You can export metrics to Datadog/Prometheus.
[45:00] Alex: Quick FAQ — common gotchas: sending full doc bodies to rerank increases payload size; pick good snippet heuristics, reduce K, offline re-ranking for low-value queries. Also pay attention to quantization if you use Dedicated infra to lower GPU costs.
[47:30] Liam: Do you have an example PoC success criteria template? We need to show business impact to leadership.
[47:50] Priya: Yes — we'll include a PoC template: baseline NDCG, latency SLO p95, cost per query target, infra plan, and success checkpoints at week 2 and week 4.
[50:10] Alex: Recap and next steps — we'll send pricing/perf spreadsheet, the rerank prompt set, security docs (SOC2/KMS/retention), and propose pilot kickoff next week.
[52:30] Sofia: Sounds good thanks.
[54:00] Raj: One last thing — can you also include sample Helm chart or k8s hints for Dedicated?
[54:45] Jordan: Yes, we'll add a short ops guide and sample Helm values to the repo link we share.
[55:00] Alex: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with artifacts.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-hearings (KV cash instead of KV cache), speaker attribution approximate, some timestamps rounded.
